newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Most pre-1945 Swiss bank funds at SBC.
newsitem.headline: Most pre-1945 Swiss bank funds at SBC.

text.p: The vast majority of the 17 million Swiss francs ($11.5 million) in new funds found in the latest sweep of pre-1945 accounts that may belong to Holocaust victims were discovered at Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), the bank said on Wednesday.
SBC said in a statement it had discovered 16 million francs since an initial search in February.
The funds had not been found previously due to an error in the way the accounts had been registered in the 1970s.
The accounts had been put onto computers at that time, but the opening dates of the accounts had not been properly filed.
The new funds were discovered when bank employees made a manual trawl through all the records.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Swiss Bankers' Association said some 17 million francs had turned up in the latest search, increasing the total amount to 60.2 million francs.

The banks said last year they had found around 43 million francs in about 1,000 accounts opened by non-Swiss before the end of World War Two and whose owners had not been heard from in at least 10 years.

Georg Krayer, chairman of the Swiss Bankers' Association, also told a news conference that the rest of the difference was due to exchange rate differences betwen the dollar and Swiss franc and by booming stock markets, which affected the value of securities held in the accounts.

Swiss banks are publishing an unprecedented three-page list of pre-1945 account-holders who may have perished in the Holocaust. The list is appearing in newspapers in 28 countries and on the Internet, breaking with a tradition of secrecy after criticism by Jewish groups.
